approach: Root cause: the critic and verifier fill a free-text `request_reading_mismatch: Option<String>`, and Athena reads any non-empty value as a misread, so "None for the plan…" counts. Fix at the agent-facing structs only. In outputs.rs, `CriticOutput` (line 535) and `VerdictOutput` (line 245) lose `request_reading_mismatch`. They gain a required `request_misread: bool` and an optional `request_misread_reason: Option<String>`. `harden` (outputs.rs:581) already lists every property as required, so the schema needs no special case. A helper `misread_explanation(Option<&str>) -> String` (trimmed text, else "no explanation given") builds the stored text. `critic_round` (planning.rs:307) sets the stored `Critique.request_reading_mismatch` only when the boolean is true, and passes the boolean to `end_round` (planning.rs:446) as an explicit argument, which branches on it. `judge` (verify.rs:625) tests `output.request_misread`. A true value with no reason still stops or fails. The stored record fields (records.rs:944, records/plan.rs:171) are unchanged, so old records, `check_record_file`, retry.rs, status.rs, status/planning.rs and display.rs keep reading the same thing. D93 (decisions.md:2078-2086) says `judge()` enforces the major rating, so the verifier path keeps its Athena-source major finding (verify.rs:632). The critic path adds no Athena finding: the critic prompt tells the critic to add the major finding itself, and `end_round` stops on the boolean either way. This revision removes the earlier run/mod.rs change. Prompts, the `M-mismatch` anchor (verify.rs:1254), the context anchors (lib.rs:605, 612) and every agent-JSON fixture move to the new keys, because both structs use `deny_unknown_fields`. The prompt edits move the computed budget lines in docs/system-facts.md, which a test enforces. The tests replay the recorded openings from pbvc and sza7 by mapping the recorded text into `request_misread_reason` with `request_misread` false. They say so in their names and comments.

decisions.choice: Keep the stored record fields `Critique.request_reading_mismatch` and `Verification.request_reading_mismatch` (Option<String>). Set them only when `request_misread` is true. Change only the agent output structs.
decisions.reason: The documented meaning at records/plan.rs:170 is 'Set when the critic judged that the accepted reading misread the request'. It fits once the field is set only on a real misread. Verification at records.rs:944 holds the same field. This leaves athena-data, old records, retry.rs:349/548/741, status.rs:137, status/planning.rs:43 and the cli readers working, and records.rs is out of scope.

rejected.option: Add a bool to the Verification and Critique records and migrate readers
rejected.why: It changes the record schema and every reader and needs a migration for old records. records.rs is out of scope.

rejected.option: Keep the free-text field and add a prefix check for 'None…'
rejected.why: It adds a string heuristic on free text. The root cause is a text field read as a flag.

decisions.choice: `end_round` gets an explicit `request_misread: bool` argument from `critic_round` and branches on it. The message text comes from the stored field (`critique.request_reading_mismatch.clone().unwrap_or_default()`) and is used only to build the stop message. `judge` tests `output.request_misread` and reads the reason only for the finding evidence, through `misread_explanation(output.request_misread_reason.as_deref())`.
decisions.reason: The brief says planning and judge act only on the yes/no field. An argument that carries the boolean makes the decision visible in the diff. The stored value is derived from the boolean, so the two cannot disagree. The stop message keeps its wording ('the critic judged that the reading misread the request: {how}'), which reading.rs:2178 and job_plan.rs:655 match on.

rejected.option: Keep `if let Some(how) = critique.request_reading_mismatch` in end_round
rejected.why: It would give the right answer today, but it tests whether text exists, which is the mistake being removed. It also fails the grep-style check in criterion 3.

decisions.choice: The critic path adds no Athena-written finding. The critic prompt tells the critic that a real misread is also a major finding, and the critic writes it. `critic_findings` and `run/mod.rs` are untouched.
decisions.reason: D93 (decisions.md:2084) puts the enforcement in `judge()`, which is the verifier path. Planning today stops on the misread in `end_round` before it looks at the verdict, with no finding added. An Athena finding with source Critic would be read by evidence_labels.rs:322-328 `findings_vote` as critic evidence, which it is not. An Athena-source finding would add a second carried copy of the text in retry.rs:741-761. Adding nothing keeps behavior unchanged, and it answers findings 10 and 11 of round 1.

rejected.option: Add a Major finding with source Critic in critic_findings (the earlier plan)
rejected.why: Athena would write text that evidence_labels counts as critic evidence, and a retry would carry the misread text twice.

rejected.option: Add the finding with source Athena
rejected.why: It still carries the text twice into a retry (retry.rs:741 and the finding loop), widens scope to run/mod.rs, and the request keeps D93 as it is.

decisions.choice: A true `request_misread` with an empty or missing reason is still a misread, with the stored text 'no explanation given'. A false one ignores any reason text and stores nothing. The CHANGELOG and decision entries name the dropped text as a known trade-off.
decisions.reason: The boolean is the single decision. The invocation record keeps no structured output (invocation.rs:145-195 records the usage, commands and detail only), so a remark sent in the reason with a false boolean is not kept. The prompts send such remarks to findings. A model that ignores that loses the remark, and this is accepted and stated openly. A model that sets true with a reason like 'None…' still stops planning: that case is rare, and the prompt asks for false and a null reason otherwise.

rejected.option: Require a non-empty reason when true and refuse the output otherwise
rejected.why: It costs a retry for a formatting lapse and adds a new refusal rule.

rejected.option: Add a minor Athena finding or ui line when a reason arrives with a false boolean
rejected.why: It adds code, a test and another finding source for a case the prompt already routes to findings. The trade-off is named in the CHANGELOG instead.

decisions.choice: The replay tests copy the recorded openings into `request_misread_reason` with `request_misread` false, and say so in their names and comments. Their claim is that an `end_round` or `judge` that tests the reason text for Some would stop or fail. A separate test shows the old key is refused.
decisions.reason: Old-format JSON no longer parses (`deny_unknown_fields` plus a required boolean), so the recorded output cannot go through the new parse unchanged. The property that matters is that the reason text no longer decides. The snapshot has no records/ directory, and the repository holds neither text (a search found no match), so only the openings quoted in the request are exact.

rejected.option: Claim the tests replay the old behavior
rejected.why: The old code would not compile against the new structs, so that claim cannot be demonstrated.

demonstrations.method: Rewrite the prompt anchor rows in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs (605 and 612) to the new sentences: `request_misread` true only for a real misread, a real misread is also a major finding, other remarks go in findings. Move the `M-mismatch` row of `REQUIRED_FIELDS` (verify.rs:1254) to anchor on `set request_misread true`, and move the test at verify.rs:3240 to replace that phrase. Then `git diff -- crates/athena-context/prompts/verifier.md` shows the net growth, which must stay under 90 tokens (270 bytes). The target is about 100 bytes, and the headroom in the facts file is 67 tokens.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-context && cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets && cargo test -p athena-core --lib verify
demonstrations.observes: The critic and verifier prompts carry the new wording. `check_verifier_prompt` accepts the shipped frame and the cap-change and cap-study fragments. The budgets test passes with the facts lines updated, and the verifier set stays at or under 1300.
demonstrations.fails_without: The lib.rs anchor test fails if a prompt lacks the new wording. `check_verifier_prompt` refuses the frame with `M-mismatch` if the anchor phrase is missing. The budgets test fails if a prompt overflows or the facts lines are stale.
demonstrations.seam: Production `compose`, `check_budget`, `check_verifier_prompt` and the prompt-anchor test in the context lib.rs, through `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` (budgets.rs:125) and the verify.rs prompt tests (verify.rs:3167-3290). All exist today. Step 8 edits the anchors and the facts lines.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff of `critic_round`, `end_round` and `judge`. `end_round` has a `request_misread: bool` parameter and an `if request_misread` branch. `critic_round` passes `critic_output.request_misread`. `judge` tests `output.request_misread`. No `if let Some(..)` or `.is_some()` test of `request_misread_reason` or of `request_reading_mismatch` decides either outcome. The reason is read only to build the message and the finding evidence.
demonstrations.observes: Both decisions branch on the boolean. The reason text is used for wording only.
demonstrations.fails_without: If either function still tested the reason text for Some, the criterion 4 and 5 replays would stop planning or fail verification.
demonstrations.seam: Not applicable: a content criterion read from the diff. Criteria 4 and 5 give the behavior proof.

demonstrations.method: New tests in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs next to the planning tests (step 11). The tests build `repo_with_planning(3)` and a `state` tempdir. They call `athena_with(&repo, &state, PASSES, crate::test_support::plenty_of_space, planning_script(vec![good_plan()], vec![critique], calls.clone()))` and then `finished_job`. The critique JSON is the pbvc critic output as the new agent writes it: verdict accept, findings with minor items only, `request_misread` false, and `request_misread_reason` starting 'None for the plan. One factual error' (recorded start from the request; the rest is reconstructed and labelled so in the comment, because records/ is absent). A second variant sets the reason to null. The tests assert `finished.state == Landed`, a non-empty `prompts_of(&calls, Role::Producer)`, and that the stored critique (from `Records::load(&athena.git, &athena.head().unwrap())`, `jobs[job.as_str()].critiques`) has `final_verdict` Accept and `request_reading_mismatch` None. They also assert that `finished.reason` lacks 'misread'.
demonstrations.observes: Planning is not stopped, the producer runs, and no misread reason is added to the job or its critique.
demonstrations.fails_without: An `end_round` or `critic_round` that tests the reason text for Some stops the job with 'the critic judged that the reading misread the request', makes no producer call, and stores the text. The three assertions on state, the producer call and the stored critique then fail. The test is a replay that maps the recorded text into the reason with the boolean false. It does not run the old code.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry `Athena::go` through `athena_with` and `finished_job` into the real `critic_round`, `CriticOutput` parse, `critic_findings`, `plan_verdict` and `end_round`. The fake agent script `planning_script` (run/tests.rs:1204) only supplies the critic JSON. It exists today. The new tests are added in step 11.

demonstrations.method: Two tests. In crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs tests, `the_sza7_reason_with_request_misread_false_adds_nothing` builds a `VerdictOutput` with `serde_json::from_value` (pass, both criteria met, no findings, `request_misread` false, `request_misread_reason` 'None for this change.', the recorded sza7 text). It calls `judge_with(&out, &["cargo test".to_string()], &[check(true)])` with the existing helpers `output()` and `check()`. It asserts `final_verdict` Pass, empty `findings`, and no reason containing 'misread the request'. In run/tests.rs, `the_sza7_verifier_text_does_not_fail_verification` wraps `base_script()` in a closure like the one in `run_planned_behavior` (run/tests.rs:1267). The closure sets `request_misread_reason` on the verifier turn and leaves the boolean false. It runs `athena_with(&repo(), ...)` and `finished_job`, and asserts Landed, no misread reason in `finished.verification.unwrap().reasons`, and `request_reading_mismatch` None in the stored verification.
demonstrations.observes: The verdict is not failed for a misread, and neither the reason 'the reading misread the request' nor a major finding is added.
demonstrations.fails_without: A `judge` that tests the reason text for Some returns Fail, adds 'the reading misread the request' and a Major finding with the sza7 text, and `check_and_verify` stores the text. Each assertion above then fails. The test maps the recorded text into the reason with the boolean false, as its name and comment say.
demonstrations.seam: Production `judge` (verify.rs:408) with the `output()` and `judge_with()` helpers (verify.rs:1935, 1958), which exist. For the second test, production `Athena::go` into `check_and_verify` (run/verification.rs, redaction at 350-377 and the stored field at 422), with a `base_script` wrapper that step 11 adds. The fake supplies only the verifier JSON.

demonstrations.method: Four tests plus one existing. In verify.rs, `a_true_request_misread_is_a_major_finding_and_the_verdict_is_not_pass` replaces the old test at verify.rs:2935. It sets `request_misread` true with a reason, and asserts Fail, a Major finding with source `FindingSource::Athena` whose evidence is the reason, and 'misread the request' in `reasons`. A sibling with no reason asserts the same with evidence 'no explanation given'. In run/tests.rs, `a_true_request_misread_stops_planning` runs `athena_with` and `planning_script` with an accept critique, `request_misread` true and a reason. It asserts Failed, a `finished.reason` containing 'the critic judged that the reading misread the request: <reason>', an empty producer prompt list, and a stored critique with `request_reading_mismatch` Some(reason). `a_true_request_misread_fails_verification` wraps the verifier turn as in criterion 5 with the boolean true, and asserts a Rejected state, the 'the reading misread the request' reason, a Major Athena finding, and the stored verification field Some(reason). The existing crates/athena-cli/tests/job_plan.rs test at line 636 still asserts 'misread the request: It reads the request as a refactor', with `critique_of` (line 462) mapping its `mismatch` argument to `request_misread` and the reason.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core a_true_request_misread && cargo test -p athena-cli --test job_plan a_reject_a_misread_reading
demonstrations.observes: With the boolean true, planning stops and verification fails, each with the misread reason, and the verification records a Major finding (D93). The critic path records no Athena finding.
demonstrations.fails_without: A `judge` or `end_round` that ignored the boolean would let a true value pass verification or continue planning. The Fail, Failed and Rejected assertions would then fail. A `judge` that dropped the finding would fail the `any(Major)` assertion.
demonstrations.seam: Same production entries as criteria 4 and 5. The `critique_of` helper and `Scenario` in job_plan.rs exist today. The job_plan.rs edit and the new tests are added in steps 10 and 11.

The test shows that a critique with a final verdict of accept and the stored field None is accepted, that the same critique with the field Some is stopped, and that a revise stays stopped. In display.rs (line 1921) the logic is unchanged: it prints the misread line only for a stored value.
